'''''Carex spicata''''' is a species of [[Carex|sedge]] in the genus ''Carex''.

==Description==
[[File:Carex spicata purple ligule.jpg|thumb|left|The purple colouring of the ligules and other basal parts, is characteristic of ''C. spicata''.]]
The [[culm (botany)|culms]] of ''Carex spicata'' are {{convert|10|-|85|cm|0}} long and approximately triangular in section.<ref name="Jermy"/> The [[leaf|leaves]] are {{convert|7|-|45|cm|0|abbr=on}} long and {{convert|2|-|4|mm|2}} wide, with a distinct keel.<ref name="Jermy"/> The [[ligule]], at the base of the leaf, is {{convert|4|-|8|mm|abbr=on}} long, with a large amount of loose white tissue.<ref name="Jermy"/> ''C. spicata'' differs from the other species in ''Carex'' section ''Phaestoglochin'' by the presence of a purple pigment in the roots, leaf sheaths and bracts.<ref name="Jermy">{{cite book |author1=A. C. Jermy |author2=D. A. Simpson |author3=M. J. Y. Foley |author4=M. S. Porter |year=2007 |title=Sedges of the British Isles |edition=3rd |series=BSBI Handbook No. 1 |isbn=978-0-901158-35-2 |publisher=[[Botanical Society of the British Isles]] |chapter=''Carex muricata'' group (section ''Phaestoglochin'' Dumort.) |pages=220–242}}</ref>

The [[inflorescence]] is {{convert|4|-|8|cm|abbr=on}} long, and comprises 3–8 [[spike (botany)|spikes]]. Each spike is {{convert|5|-|10|mm|abbr=on}} long, with female (pistillate) flowers at the base, and male (staminate) flowers at the tip.<ref name="Jermy"/>

==Distribution and ecology==
''Carex spicata'' has a European temperate distribution, although it has been extensively [[Naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] outside this native range.<ref name="OABIF">{{cite web |url=http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=plant/carex-spicata |title=''Carex spicata'' (Spiked Sedge) |work=Online Atlas of the British & Irish Flora |publisher=[[Biological Records Centre]] |accessdate=July 7, 2011}}</ref>

''Carex spicata'' is usually found in [[grassland]] (usually in [[British NVC community MG10]] in the British Isles), on roadsides, and in waste ground.<ref name="Jermy"/> It is found on heavy, slightly base-rich soils, and cannot tolerate much [[competition (biology)|competition]].<ref name="OABIF"/>

==Taxonomy==
''Carex spicata'' was [[species description|first described]] by the English botanist [[William Hudson (botanist)|William Hudson]] in his 1762 work ''[[Flora Anglica]]''.<ref>{{cite book |author=William Hudson |author-link=William Hudson (botanist) |year=1762 |title=Flora Anglica |language=Latin |chapter=''Carex'' |pages=346–354 |publisher=Londini, impensis auctoris |chapter-url=https://archive.org/stream/gulielmihudsoni01hudsgoog#page/n370/mode/2up}}</ref>

It is known in the [[British Isles]] as "spiked sedge",<ref name="Jermy"/><ref name="Stace">{{Cite book |author=Clive A. Stace |author-link=Clive A. Stace |year=2010 |title=New Flora of the British Isles |url=https://archive.org/details/newflorabritishi00stac |url-access=limited |edition=3rd |chapter=''Carex'' L. – sedges |pages=[https://archive.org/details/newflorabritishi00stac/page/n986 951]–974 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |isbn=978-0-521-70772-5}}</ref> in North America as "spicate sedge"<ref>{{Cite book |author=Robert H. Mohlenbrock |year=2011 |title=Sedges: ''Carex'' |series=The Illustrated Flora of Illinois |edition=2nd |publisher=[[Southern Illinois University Press]] |isbn=978-0-8093-3024-9 |chapter=''Carex spicata'' |chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=NOA4mUNE7y8C&pg=PA57 |pages=57–59}}</ref> or "prickly sedge".<ref>{{cite web |url=https://plants.usda.gov/java/profile?symbol=CASP10 |title=''Carex spicata'' Huds. prickly sedge |work=PLANTS Profile |access-date=July 7, 2011 |publisher=[[United States Department of Agriculture]]}}</ref> In [[Irish language|Irish]] it is called ''{{lang|ga|cíb spícíneach}}'',<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.species.ie/search/species/detail/?species_id=6654 |title=''Carex spicata'' Huds. |work=The Irish Species Register |date=October 16, 2008 |author=Wendy Guiry |accessdate=July 7, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111009013742/http://www.species.ie/search/species/detail/?species_id=6654 |archive-date=October 9, 2011 |url-status=dead }}</ref> and in [[Welsh language|Welsh]], its name is ''{{lang|cy|hesgen dywysennog borffor}}'',<ref>{{cite journal|author=G. Battershall |year=2000 |title=Welsh Plant Records 1998 |journal=Welsh Bulletin |publisher=[[Botanical Society of the British Isles]] |volume=67 |pages=26–30 |url=http://www.watsonia.org.uk/WBULL67.pdf |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120321174111/http://www.watsonia.org.uk/WBULL67.pdf |archivedate=2012-03-21 }}</ref> ''{{lang|cy|hesgen dywysennog}}''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.gardenofwales.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2011/02/List-of-plant-names-for-website-1.pdf |title=List of plant names |publisher=[[National Botanic Garden of Wales ]] |accessdate=July 7, 2011 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110926224941/http://www.gardenofwales.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2011/02/List-of-plant-names-for-website-1.pdf |archivedate=September 26, 2011 }}</ref> or ''{{lang|cy|hesgen ysbigog borffor}}''.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.eu-nomen.eu/portal/taxon.php?GUID=3B46B284-E2D6-4C42-A7C4-0592BA5B14AA |date=February 7, 2011 |author1=P. Jiménez-Mejías |author2=M. Luceño |title=''Carex spicata'' Huds. |work=Pan-European Species directories Infrastructure |accessdate=July 7, 2011}}</ref>

Few [[hybrid (biology)|hybrids]] have been reported between ''C. spicata'' and other members of ''Carex'' sect. ''Phaestoglochin'', but hybrids have been reported between ''C. spicata'' and ''[[Carex otrubae|C. otrubae]]'', and between ''C. spicata'' and ''[[Carex echinata|C. echinata]]''.<ref name="Jermy"/>
